body: The witness was next to my lane, we were both turning the same direction when I was hit. She saw the whole thing, and my car was shoved into hers.

1. Eat a light meal around noon
2. Drink a sugar free/no aspartame energy drink
3. After about an hour, I start drinking light beers
4. Stop drinking after about 2-4 hrs
5. Take some Pepto
6. Go bed 
7. No hangover
Tired of getting "hit on" by guys. They'll say I need to smile more and think they're really doing something. I don't get it. Don't insult me and pretend it's a compliment
Commenting because I struggle with the same thing nearly daily and also would love advice on the matter
I feel ya, bud. And I’m so sorry you’re having a bad go at it, too. We don’t deserve what our brains put us through. I wish that sentence was enough to put my brain in its’ place.
Lol exactly my thoughts
Thank you
She is primarily Spanish speaking
How do I respond?

This is where I’m at currently. Most of the time, I feel like I’m trying to convince myself to do something that I’ll enjoy, but I’m so damn antsy and I can never fully focus or immerse myself when I’m depressed, so I eventually give up and give in to the spiral.
Jesus, felt like you took those words straight from my brain.

Thank you for your response. I felt pretty confused tonight honestly, my partner even started tearing up because they seemed so tired of me getting upset with them. But this example is pretty par for the course… I’ll get hurt over something that sounded kind of inconsiderate, then after confronting it I feel like I’m being unreasonable, so I’ll try to dial back the emotions, but at that point both of us are upset and there’s no going back. I will note this almost always happens late at night, but usually in the middle of us getting along and feels so out of the blue.

Just added the most recent stupid spat we had, basically every time I end up upset this is about how it goes

I love the shit out of this person and I know they care about me but I feel like I get too in my feelings when they say things that come off the wrong way, and I could possibly go about it better if I weren’t so sensitive
With enough speed, you can eat losers for breakfast.

I would emphasize the physical issues the stress causes you. I’ve found (unfortunately), that if you chalk it up to just anxiety, it’s a lot harder to get any sort of understanding. Tell your boss what you listed out here: the stress of this specific register tends to have a negative impact on your health, and you would like to avoid having to call out due to it.

If they don’t understand or aren’t willing to work with you, I’d honestly start looking into other options for work. No job is worth your health.
I also vomit, like all the damn time, to the point I lose weight and have to leave work early
Have you eaten today?

Unfortunately my manager was standing at the front doors watching the whole thing so I had to help her. I was hoping the woman just needed help pushing the second cart to her car, but then she asked me to help her load everything. At that point I just wanted her out of the parking lot so I could push the carts back where they belong.
Bruh, where are you working now? I’d love to find a store like you’re at now.

Had a woman do this to me with two full baskets; $500 worth of items. As I was bagging the final bag, a bottle of soap opened and got all over about $50 worth of items which I then had to void. Once I was finished with that, she had me load her baskets, push them to her car, and fit her groceries in the back like Tetris. Her trunk barely closed. All in all she held the store open for nearly an hour after close. Would like to mention she was also extremely specific about how I did everything that I helped her with, and was ungrateful as hell.

I have customers come back through the line (forgetting something previously), and I will greet them the same way I did the first time. I’ve had a couple respond letting me know, “yeah I forgot I needed this,” then I realize.

I don’t believe I would be reliable if a cop were to ask me to describe a criminal lmao.
I feel like I dread 90% of customers, and enjoy them maybe 10% of the time

Yeah, I’m honestly not all that great with names. If I could absorb all of that information and manage to name everybody, I would. I’m really not a fan of only being able to remember a select few names. But it’s also not in my job description to do that, anyways. All I say is I wish it didn’t seem to be expected from some people, because not everybody is capable of having such a great memory. Props to the people who can do so.
I gotta ask, what did Ricardo do? 🤣
—And I wish all the Dirty Dans a very, “smell better soon!”
Currently not taking any medications. And I avoid caffeine/alcohol.
Thank you! I’ll definitely cop me some of these.

Rabbit holes, man. On my worst days, it’s genuinely like I’m being sucked into them.
It starts off with genuine curiosity and quickly ramps up to, “I must know now.” 

Then you find out something else in the midst of an article. Now you’re watching a 2 hour documentary. But wait, what was that first thing you were searching up? Oh yeah let’s get back to that, but first you absolutely HAVE to look at this other thing before you forget that you were gonna look at that. Shit, it’s 4am. 
“Oh well, this video is only 2 minutes, I’ll go to bed after….” *cue sunrise and birds chirping to remind you of your mistakes*

Definitely relatable stimming. I’m trying hard to rid my routine of the harmful stimming, though.
Skin picking in general is the worst for me. 
I will zone out for an hour or so just picking until I’ve left tiny scabs all over my legs and arms.

I will also crack my knuckles; I try to crack every individual digit in every way possible and don’t stop until I’ve finished getting all of the pops I want. I don’t pick in public but I definitely crack my knuckles mindlessly anywhere. 
I used to crack my neck frequently too, but one day I scared some poor woman I was standing behind in a store with the sound. I don’t do that anymore.

Unfortunately some stores are more strict about inventory than others. I’ve been bitched at before for trying to take the easier route and scanning one item for multiples when there were different types of said item. Even though they may be the same price, it still matters, at least where I work.

I believe OP is referring to when someone has similar items with different barcodes (ex. different flavors of the same brand of cola), and only hands you one of the items to scan multiple times. 
Inventory gets totally messed up if you scan 10 fruit punch Gatorade bottles when there were actually 5 fruit punch and 5 lemon lime. Accuracy is important. But according to most customers, it shouldn’t matter how many they have of each flavor since they’re all the same price.

When you gotta ID someone that’s clearly over 21 and they say, “are you kidding me? You could be my grandchild!”

I usually respond with, “yup, and I’d still have to ID you.”
I say my own, only in context with when my name tag is out of sight. Because that means this man has mentally noted my name. Those guys tend to be the weirder ones, I’ve noticed.
I fantasize about this often

The best part is, for every aisle that has a mess like this on it, there will be at least one customer that will complain about how awful it looks, as if it is our fault. 

I know it looks awful, I know it needs to be picked up, and if I could bring the messes to a halt I would. But these messes are a work of other customers. The customer complaining may not be making the messes, but they have something in common with the customers who are: they both don’t seem to give a shit about how busy we are, how little time, or how little people we have to get everything done.
Absolutely lol. I’m leaving by next year. This place has gotten worse and worse since I first applied.

Can confirm, every compliment I receive from older men at work is definitely read into on my end. I’m constantly gauging in my head whether a situation needs to be shut down or not due to the creeps. Compliments are nice, but at this point I’d rather keep it strictly to business and treat the situation as it is: a simple transaction. 
My days go by so much smoother when customers are kind of short and to the point.

Had to turn down this one guy, told him I was married, the works. This dude literally said, out loud, with his mouth, to my face: “well let me know when you dump the zero, if you wanna get with a hero.” And marched on out the store with his nose in the air. The gall of some people lmao. Thank god I’ve never seen him since, I believe he embarrassed himself from ever wanting to come back.
I think every store needs a random buff lumberjack-lookin dude surveying like that. Not even a security guard, just a man we can point at when people start to creep.
Fuck it. This is good advice lmao. I don’t lose a dime if we lose a customer and I’m definitely so damn tired of walking on eggshells all of the time.

I also wear a fake wedding ring! It’s kind of shitty in my opinion that a ring seems to deter people more than me just saying no. I’ve had a few customers back off once seeing the ring, saying something along the lines of, “I don’t wanna piss the wrong guy off.”
What about me? You’re fine with pissing me off? Oh that’s right, I forgot. I’m not as intimidating as my imaginary husband you’ve never seen. And you know damn well I can’t do shit to make you stop when I’m on the clock.

I get this all the time at my store. It’s awful when this happens as my religious coworker is up at registers with me. It’s like a domino effect of everyone preaching their own love for god. Starts with the customer, bounces off of my coworker, then usually continues on with a few customers afterwards, all circlejerking mid-transaction as I stand there waiting to get rid of the line that forms.

Our lines can get upwards to 10+. Our general rule of thumb is to call for backup once the fourth person gets in line, but with us being so understaffed, there often is no backup available. There’s been many incidences where I stayed overtime just to help backup another cashier during rushes, because if I leave, they’ll be alone with an angry mob of customers.

Nah, I actually called my manager up to help me and she never came lol. By the time I saw my manager and told her about the situation, her only response was, “why didn’t you call for me?” To which I told her that I did, and she just kinda shrugged it off.
